newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: IMF mission to visit Kazakhstan next week.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission to visit Kazakhstan next week.

text.p: A mission from the International Monetary Fund will visit Kazakhstan next week to assess the oil-rich republic's economic reforms under a $446 million loan from the Fund, an IMF official said on Tuesday.
"The mission is coming to evaluate progress under the extended fund facility," the IMF's resident representative in Kazakhstan, David Hoelscher, told Reuters.
He said the visit is the first since the IMF agreed to a $446 million three-year loan in July.
Under the programme, Kazakhstan will aim for 0.4-percent economic growth this year, 0.9 percent in 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998.
The former Soviet republic's economy contracted 8.9 percent in 1995 and 25 percent in 1994. This year's annual inflation target is near 27.5 percent.
Last month, Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev promised the "harshest measures" to close down bankrupt enterprises and establish single-digit inflation by the end of the decade.
But the 16.9 million people there are growing impatient with unpaid salaries and pensions while energy shortages threaten a cold winter.
